translationRepairs: On jiwei, the Right Thousand-Bull Upper General Sun Hanyun was appointed prefect of Jiang Prefecture.
On jiyou, the Right Thousand-Bull Upper General Sun Hanyun was appointed prefect of Jiang Prefecture.

Focus unit opens with 己酉; that sexagenary day is jiyou, not jiwei (己未). Neighboring 丙午 and 辛亥 confirm the sequence, so the proposed day-name correction is required and otherwise leaves the sentence intact.
On jiwei, the Right Thousand-Bull Upper General Sun Hanyun was made prefect of Jiang Prefecture.
On jiyou, the Right Thousand-Bull Upper General Sun Hanyun was made prefect of Jiang Prefecture.
The Chinese date is 己酉 (jiyou). Rendering it as jiwei misreads the earthly branch 酉 as 未; the proposed literal fix restores the correct day name without other changes.

On jiwei, Liu Xin of Xuzhou was given the additional title of Palace Attendant, Kaifeng intendant Hou Yi was advanced to Duke of Lu, and Murong Yanchao of Yunzhou and Liu Zhu of Qing Prefecture were both given the additional title of Palace Attendant.

On jiwei, Liu Xin of Xu Prefecture was given the additional title of Palace Attendant, Kaifeng intendant Hou Yi was advanced to Duke of Lu, and Murong Yanchao of Yunzhou and Liu Zhu of Qing Prefecture were both given the additional title of Palace Attendant.
Focus unit has 許州劉信; 許州 is Xu Prefecture and must not be rendered as Xuzhou (徐州). The rest of the proposed sentence matches the Chinese, including 己未 as jiwei.

On jiwei, Xuzhou Liu Xin was given the additional title of Palace Attendant; Kaifeng intendant Hou Yi was advanced to Duke of Lu; Yunzhou Murong Yanchao and Qing Prefecture Liu Zhu were both given the additional title of Palace Attendant.

On jiwei, Xu Prefecture Liu Xin was given the additional title of Palace Attendant; Kaifeng intendant Hou Yi was advanced to Duke of Lu; Yunzhou Murong Yanchao and Qing Prefecture Liu Zhu were both given the additional title of Palace Attendant.
Literal English wrongly places Liu Xin at Xuzhou; the Chinese place is 許州, so Xu Prefecture is the accurate replacement and no other semantic change is introduced.
On dingsi, Li Hongxin of Chanzong was transferred to Shan Prefecture, and the Imperial Guard cavalry commander and Suizhou military governor Li Hongyi was appointed military governor of Chanzong.

On dingsi, Li Hongxin of Chan Prefecture was transferred to Shan Prefecture, and the Imperial Guard cavalry commander and Suizhou military governor Li Hongyi was appointed military governor of Chan Prefecture.
Focus unit twice names 澶州; that prefecture is Chan Prefecture, and Chanzong is not a valid reading. Both occurrences in the idiomatic sentence need the proposed correction.
On dingsi, Chanzong Li Hongxin was transferred to Shan Prefecture; the Imperial Guard cavalry commander and Suizhou military governor Li Hongyi was made military governor of Chanzong.
On dingsi, Chan Prefecture Li Hongxin was transferred to Shan Prefecture; the Imperial Guard cavalry commander and Suizhou military governor Li Hongyi was made military governor of Chan Prefecture.
The literal likewise mistranslates 澶州 as Chanzong; Chan Prefecture restores the place name in both mentions without altering offices or persons.
On dingmao, the former Luozhou regiment-training commissioner Wu Hanqiu died.
On dingmao, the former Ming Prefecture regiment-training commissioner Wu Hanqiu died.
Focus unit has 前洺州團練使; 洺州 is Ming Prefecture, not Luozhou (洛州). The proposed idiomatic replacement corrects that place name and leaves the rest accurate.
On dingmao, the former Luozhou regiment-training commissioner Wu Hanqiu died.
On dingmao, the former Ming Prefecture regiment-training commissioner Wu Hanqiu died.
Literal English likewise misreads 洺州 as Luozhou; Ming Prefecture is the correct English for 洺州 and the proposed fix is otherwise faithful.
